dc.description.abstract.value:
Summary of the Apprentices Act, 1961 
The Apprentices Act, 1961 was enacted to regulate and promote apprenticeship training in industries across India. The Act aims to develop a skilled workforce by providing practical, industry-based training to apprentices under the supervision of employers. It lays down the framework for the engagement of apprentices, the responsibilities of employers and apprentices, and the standards for apprenticeship training. The Act has been amended from time to time, most notably in 2014, to make apprenticeship training more flexible and industry-oriented.
Objective
The main objectives of the Act are:
•	To regulate the training of apprentices in designated and optional trades.
•	To develop a skilled workforce to meet the needs of industry.
•	To bridge the gap between theoretical education and practical training.
•	To prescribe the rights, duties, and obligations of employers and apprentices.
•	To promote employment opportunities through skill development and vocational training.
Key Provisions
1.	Engagement of Apprentices
o	Employers in specified establishments are required or permitted to engage apprentices in accordance with the provisions of the Act and the rules made thereunder.
2.	Apprenticeship Contract
o	Every apprenticeship is governed by a contract of apprenticeship entered into between the employer and the apprentice, which must be registered in the prescribed manner.
3.	Eligibility
o	Prescribes eligibility criteria relating to age, educational qualifications, and physical fitness for undergoing apprenticeship training.
4.	Duration of Training
o	The period of apprenticeship training varies according to the designated or optional trade and is prescribed by the Central Government.
5.	Practical and Basic Training
o	Employers are required to provide practical training, while basic training may be arranged through approved training institutes where necessary.
6.	Stipend
o	Apprentices are entitled to receive a stipend during the training period at rates prescribed by the Central Government or as mutually agreed, subject to statutory minimum requirements.
7.	Responsibilities of Employers
o	Employers must provide proper training facilities, qualified instructors, safe working conditions, and maintain records relating to apprenticeship training.
8.	Duties of Apprentices
o	Apprentices are required to learn diligently, follow lawful instructions, maintain discipline, and attend training regularly.
9.	Assessment and Certification
o	Upon successful completion of training and the prescribed assessment, apprentices are awarded certificates recognizing their vocational skills.
10.	Dispute Resolution
•	The Act provides for the resolution of disputes between employers and apprentices through the designated apprenticeship authorities.
11.	Penalties
•	Prescribes penalties for employers who fail to comply with the provisions of the Act or violate their statutory obligations.
12.	Apprentices Not Treated as Employees
•	Apprentices undergoing training under the Act are trainees and are generally not considered workers or employees for the purposes of labour laws, except where specifically provided.

(2) The Director, Board of Examinations and Evaluation shall be appointed by the Vice-Chancellor from amongst faculty member of the university on the recommendation of a selection committee constituted for the purpose, as prescribed in the Statues.
(3) The term of Director, Board of Examinations and Evaluation shall be five years or till he attains the age of superannuation, whichever is earlier:

(4) The Director, Board of Examinations and Evaluation shall,-
(a) be the principal officer-in-charge of the conduct of the university examinations, tests and evaluation, and declaration of their results;
(b) be the Member-Secretary of the Board of Examinations and Evaluation;
(c) be responsible for making all arrangements necessary for holding examinations, tests and evaluation, and for timely declaration of results;
(d) evolve and implement in consultation with the Examinations and Evaluation Cell, processes for proper and smooth conduct of examinations and evaluation;
(e) prepare and announce in advance the programme of examinations, after seeking approval of the Board of Examinations and Evaluation;
(f) postpone or cancel examinations, in part or in whole, in the event of malpractices or if the circumstances so warrant, and take disciplinary action or initiate any civil or criminal proceedings against any person or a group of persons alleged to have committed malpractices, with approval of the Vice-Chancellor;
(g) take disciplinary action wherever necessary against the candidates, paper setters, examiners, moderators, or any other persons connected with examinations and evaluation, found guilty of malpractices in relation to the examinations and evaluation;
(h) strive to declare the results of every examination and evaluation conducted by the university within fifteen days from the last date of the examination for that particular course and shall in any case declare the results as provided in section 55 and in case of delay, prepare detailed report outlining the reasons;
(i) take all steps for implementation of all academic and administrative decisions taken by the Board of Examinations and Evaluation;
(j) implement decisions taken by the various university authorities, connected with the examination and evaluation process;
(k) implement all policy and operative decisions with reference to the choice based credit system, at the under-graduate, post-graduate levels and in other teaching programmes;
(l) organize workshops for teachers in the subjects concerned, in order to acquaint them with new trends in the assessment processes, such as cognitive and summative assessment, creation and use of repository of questions, use of technology in paper setting and conduct of examinations, tests and evaluation;
(m) ensure innovative and effective use of information and communication technology in the entire process of the conduct of examinations and evaluation;
(n) arrange for proper assessment of performance of candidates at the examinations and process the results;
(o) ensure that answer books for all examinations are assessed through a mechanism and system, as prescribed in the Ordinances;
(p) ensure that every teacher and non-teaching employee in the university, renders necessary assistance and service in respect of examinations of the university and in evaluation process;
(q) carry out all other duties and functions assigned to him by the Board of Examinations and Evaluation;
(r) undertake any other task assigned to him by the university authorities to carry out the objectives of the Board of Examinations and Evaluations, and to ensure that the objects of the university are accomplished;
